column2: req_desc

Builder steps and mirror
The workout builder offers the five step kinds with the published defaults and limits, and it shows every step both in the drawn graph and in a Steps list that exposes each part's kind, duration and target as text and attributes.

Builder keyboard editing
With the Steps list focused, the published keys select, resize, retarget, repeat, reorder and delete steps, and each change is announced with the published text.

Planned stress totals
The builder's duration, planned TSS and planned IF follow the published formula and display rules, and they update on every change.

Saving and placing built workouts
A built workout saves to a calendar day or to the library, a library workout can be placed on a day by drag or keyboard, and the result is still there after a reload.

Builder graph dragging
With a mouse or touch, dragging a step's right edge changes its duration and dragging its top edge changes its target, each snapped and clamped as published.

Moving planned workouts
A planned workout moves to another day by drag or by keyboard pick-up and drop with the published announcements, and the server refuses the illegal moves with the published statuses.

Week totals and tally
Each week shows planned and completed TSS totals, the six-state compliance tally and the week's form, computed by the published rules.

Live calendar updates
Any change to an athlete's workouts, thresholds or links appears in every other open view of that athlete within 3 seconds without a reload.

Activity file format
Uploads accept the published CSV and JSON activity formats, with 1-Hz samples starting at t = 0.

Power stress scoring
A ride file is scored with the published normalised power, IF and TSS formulas against the FTP in force on its day.

Storage-confirmed uploads
An upload becomes a completed workout only after storage confirms the stored object's size and SHA-256, as qualified in Services.

Planned versus completed
Every calendar item carries one of the six published compliance states, decided by the published ratio bands and same-day matching rule.

Effective-dated thresholds
A threshold applies from its effective date, and adding one re-scores exactly the completed workouts in its span and recomputes the series from its first day.

Run stress scoring
A run file or manual run is scored with the published normalised speed, IF and rTSS formulas against the threshold pace in force on its day.

Athlete-local dates
Workout dates, week boundaries, totals and the stress series always follow the athlete's own time zone, whoever is viewing.

Server-decided missed state
Planned and missed states come only from the server's configured today, and a wrong device clock changes nothing on screen.

Daily fitness series
The server stores one daily fitness, fatigue and form series per athlete, computed by the published formulas and recomputed whenever its inputs change.

Fitness chart and table
The fitness chart card draws the stored series with the centred week highlighted, mirrors it in a table, and lets the keyboard step a focus marker day by day with the published announcement.

Chart animation timing
Chart changes animate for the configured chart duration with motion, and apply at once with reduced motion.

Deleting workouts
Deleting a workout removes its row, its stored file and its stress in one step, or nothing at all.

Numbers agree everywhere
After any upload, entry, move, delete or re-score, the calendar, week rail, tiles, banner, chart and table show the same values as the API, also after a reload.

Activity file checks
A refused file is checked in the published order, answers the published status and message, and creates nothing.

Upload error display
A refused upload shows the server's message in an alert that receives focus, and it keeps the dialog open with the file still selected.

Plan templates and rest weeks
A plan template is a numbered run of days, and every fourth week is applied as a rest week at the published share of duration.

Applying plans
A coach applies a plan from a start date or counts it back from an event date, days that have passed are skipped, and the published confirmation reports what was created, skipped and kept.

Wall-clock start times
Planned start times are stored as local wall-clock times, so a clock change keeps 06:30 at 06:30 under the published gap and overlap rule.

Copy week dialog
The Copy week dialog supports keyboard multi-select, keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside itself, closes on Escape and returns focus to its opener.

Copying to another athlete
Copying planned workouts to another linked athlete keeps their weekdays and start times, scores them with the target athlete's thresholds and skips days that have passed.

Coach dashboard
The coach's athlete list shows each linked athlete's week totals and latest session, and a new session updates it in place within 3 seconds.

Workout comments and notices
Comments on a workout appear for both parties within 3 seconds, with the published in-app notice.

Original file download
Downloading a completed workout's original returns exactly the uploaded bytes, with the SHA-256 the workout detail shows.

Coach link requests
A coach code creates a link request that the coach accepts or declines before it expires, following the published state machine.

Not found for unshared data
Anything a user may not open answers 404 as a page and in the API, never 403, and the published error-check order applies everywhere.

Removing a coach
When an athlete removes a coach, the coach loses access on their next request, and the coach's open views switch to the not-found view within 3 seconds.

Manual session entry
A hand-entered session is validated with the published messages and scored with the published average-based formulas.

Phone calendar
At phone width the calendar, its week rail and Log a session work by touch, with no horizontal overflow.

Storage outage
With storage unreachable, health reports unavailable, uploads and downloads refuse with the published outage message, and manual entry still works.

Grading route
A key-protected seed and reset route creates and clears the published records and returns their ids and one-time sign-in links.

Health and boot
The health endpoint and boot behaviour follow the published responses and schema-on-serve rule.

Sign-in and sessions
Users sign in with email and password or a one-time link, and they hold a session until they sign out.

Week peek rail
The week peek rail advances by button, arrow key, swipe or dot with the published motion, address update, chart band move and announcement, and it swaps instantly with reduced motion.

Home sections
The today form banner, weekly sport total tiles, compliance ring rows, recent uploads drift wall and event countdown band show the published values.

Look and feel
Every screen carries the published visual direction: the solid cobalt today band, navy pills, near-white ground, white rounded tiles and wide extra-bold numerals.

Responsive layouts
Every screen works at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800 with no horizontal overflow and tap targets at least 44 px.

Configuration from environment
Every service URL, credential, limit, timer and clock setting is read from the published environment variables, never hard-coded and never sent to the browser.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1".
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) and every bundled font, each with its licence.
Shipped packages and fonts use only MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, BlueOak-1.0.0, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1 licences.
package-lock.json is committed and matches package.json.
No datastore or service is used beyond the provided PostgreSQL and object storage.
The provided development service configuration and credentials are left unchanged.
The source contains no other product's name, logo, photo or copied marketing text, and pages load no external fonts, images or scripts.
